findings.title: Possible Misattribution
findings.body: The agent is taken from the thread's earliest comment, but the "owner" shown after it comes from `props.author`, the row's own author. If the toolkit's list row shows a different author than the thread starter, the row combines two people. For example, an agent thread started by max and last replied to by bob would read "Claude / bob" with bob's avatar badged. The pin avoids this by using `thread.createdBy`. Worth confirming which author `CommentListItem` receives. If it is not always the thread creator, resolve the owner from `thread.createdBy` (via `ResolveCommentAuthorContext`) as `TlaPinContent` does.

findings.title: Browser Support
findings.body: The `focusVisible: false` option of `focus()` is not supported in every browser (Chromium has not shipped it, as far as I know); browsers without it ignore the option. When an edit is closed with the keyboard (e.g. Escape or Enter), the browser's heuristics will still mark the returned focus as `:focus-visible`. Combined with the new `.tlui-cmt-card:has(:focus-visible)` rule, the card's actions then stay visible after the pointer leaves, which is the behaviour this change aims to prevent.

Possible Misattribution
The agent is taken from the thread's earliest comment, but the "owner" shown after it comes from `props.author`, the row's own author. If the toolkit's list row shows a different author than the thread starter, the row combines two people. For example, an agent thread started by max and last replied to by bob would read "Claude / bob" with bob's avatar badged. The pin avoids this by using `thread.createdBy`. Worth confirming which author `CommentListItem` receives. If it is not always the thread creator, resolve the owner from `thread.createdBy` (via `ResolveCommentAuthorContext`) as `TlaPinContent` does. Browser Support
The `focusVisible: false` option of `focus()` is not supported in every browser (Chromium has not shipped it, as far as I know); browsers without it ignore the option. When an edit is closed with the keyboard (e.g. Escape or Enter), the browser's heuristics will still mark the returned focus as `:focus-visible`. Combined with the new `.tlui-cmt-card:has(:focus-visible)` rule, the card's actions then stay visible after the pointer leaves, which is the behaviour this change aims to prevent.
